title: Commercial transfer screen for the rooted-MAF campaign
scope: Focused opportunity research. No novelty clearance, commercial demand validation, solver benchmark, financial backtest, or medical performance evaluation was performed.
conclusion: A published grasp-taxonomy method already calls rooted MAF. Finance and cybersecurity offer concrete topology-comparison inputs, but the proposed product value remains untested.
mapping_requirements: Two rooted binary trees on an identical, uniquely identified leaf set.
Internal child order is irrelevant; each leaf denotes the same entity in both inputs.
The requested objective is minimum-component agreement under equal rooted restrictions and vertex-disjoint embeddings.
If only topology is compared, branch heights, numerical values and internal-node labels are deliberately outside the objective.
Unequal universes require an explicitly restricted common-universe question; additions and removals are reported separately.
Arbitrary binary refinements of multifurcations do not establish an equivalent reduction.
Using the forest result as an rSPR distance requires matching the root-augmentation convention and reconstruction interface.
A lower exponential base must be measured at the actual disagreement parameter and compared with current solvers.

opportunities.problem: Accelerate pairwise rooted-MAF calls inside SPR supertree construction for hand-grasp taxonomies.
opportunities.evidence_grade: Existing published rooted-MAF subroutine; commercial speedup unmeasured.
opportunities.read_facts: Stival et al. describe merging subject/feature grasp trees with SPR supertrees and explicitly identify rooted-MAF computation in Methods, printed page 6.
opportunities.mapping: Grasp identifiers become leaf labels. Preserve the rooted binary topology of each pair requested by the existing supertree procedure; supply compatible forest/distance outputs under its root convention.
opportunities.prospective_buyer: Robotic-hand, prosthetics and rehabilitation-device R&D teams; no buyer contacted.
opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: Paid integration or R&D software could reduce repeated taxonomy-reconstruction work if MAF remains a material runtime component.
limits: The study used 20 grasps; an existing modern solver may already be fast enough.
Speeding the pairwise primitive does not solve global supertree optimization.
No controller, clinical or patient outcome improvement follows from a solver timing improvement.
opportunities.first_decisive_test: Recover the original pairwise calls, profile a current rSPR baseline, and benchmark replacement under identical conventions. Stop commercialization of the speedup if pairwise solving is negligible.

opportunities.problem: Explain structural changes in asset-clustering hierarchies across rolling windows, covariance estimators or resamples.
opportunities.evidence_grade: Direct input encoding for a proposed diagnostic metric; no established MAF deployment or revenue demonstrated.
opportunities.read_facts: skfolio documents asset linkage matrices and an allocator, HERC, that uses dendrogram shape. PortfolioLab lists clustering models and paid licensing.
opportunities.mapping: Fix asset IDs. Convert each linkage merge into a binary node, retaining asset IDs at leaves. Compare the two resulting topologies with ordinary rooted MAF. The output minimizes fragmentation into common disjoint structural pieces.
opportunities.prospective_buyer: Quantitative portfolio research and risk-model teams, or portfolio-analytics software vendors; no buyer contacted.
opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: Sell an explanation/reporting component if it improves investigation of hierarchy instability or avoids unnecessary review/rebalancing decisions.
limits: The forest is not an optimal portfolio, trade sequence, turnover minimizer or profit predictor.
The topology-only objective discards correlation magnitudes and clustering heights.
MAF distance has not been shown here to predict turnover or losses.
Cheaper split, triplet, cophenetic, covariance and allocation-change measures may answer the customer's question sufficiently.
This introduces a diagnostic; it does not accelerate the existing clustering or allocation algorithm.
opportunities.first_decisive_test: Use fixed-universe rolling/resampled hierarchies from skfolio's documented example data. Compare diagnostic usefulness with cheap alternatives before investing in a faster exact solver. Measure runtime, actual k, explanation usefulness and decision value separately.

opportunities.problem: Find common structural fragments and conflicts between alternative malware lineage reconstructions over the same sample IDs.
opportunities.evidence_grade: Rooted binary inputs can be supplied by existing methods; MAF diagnostic and commercial benefit are proposed.
opportunities.read_facts: MalTree supplies UPGMA/NJ phylogenies and sample identifiers linked to hashes. Its paper distinguishes rooted UPGMA from NJ requiring rooting.
opportunities.mapping: Use the same malware sample hashes in both trees. Compare two rooted binary feature/model reconstructions; ordinary MAF returns a minimum-component common forest. Validate rooting and binary structure before admitting a pair.
opportunities.prospective_buyer: Threat-intelligence vendors, malware-analysis teams and managed security providers; no buyer contacted.
opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: An analyst-facing comparison component could prioritize inconsistent family assignments or feature/model disagreements and reduce manual investigation.
limits: Inconsistency between feature trees does not prove code borrowing or attacker attribution.
No speedup of embedding extraction, tree construction or endpoint malware detection is established.
Whole-dataset highly discordant trees may have a prohibitive k despite a better exponential base.
Use per-family/nearby-version pairs first; do not infer tractability from leaf count alone.
opportunities.first_decisive_test: Use released trees or metadata/embeddings, without acquiring or executing malware binaries. Form explicit same-universe rooted pairs, compare with rSPR and cheap topology baselines, then measure analyst utility on labelled cases.

downgraded_or_rejected.finding: Conditional research idea, not a direct replacement for the published classifier.
downgraded_or_rejected.reason: The commercial source uses category paths and cascading clustering. A general retail taxonomy need not be binary, leaf universes can differ, and semantic/revenue-weighted migration costs are absent from ordinary MAF. A restricted same-SKU binary-dendrogram audit is input-compatible, but its business usefulness is untested.

A promising peer-selection source was found but its full text could not be opened in the final targeted retrieval. No reduction is claimed; numeric balances, internal-node semantics and unequal trees must not be silently discarded.
The documented optimization chooses trades using return, risk, holding and transaction-cost inputs. Comparing topology via MAF does not solve that decision problem.
Order, internal-node labels, insertions/deletions and repeated labels can carry semantics excluded by the campaign's ordinary rooted-MAF model.

evaluation_order: First test the existing grasp-taxonomy subroutine for a meaningful remaining bottleneck.
For finance, test whether exact structural fragments improve decisions or explanations over inexpensive metrics.
For cybersecurity, validate analyst benefit and actual parameter sizes on family-level cases.
Only after application value is established compare candidate/current solver wall time, memory and witness validity.
gaps: Focused English-language web search through 2026-10-15, not an exhaustive literature or novelty review.
